summary: This article explains how owls use their large eyes, flexible necks, sharp hearing, and silent feathers to hunt at night, and why farmers in Saudi Arabia welcome them.
introduce: Show the title “Owls of the Night” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: awake and active at night instead of during the day
one kind of animal or plant
the long, sharp, curved claws of a bird that hunts

challengeTerms.def: an animal that hunts and eats other animals
the small bones that form the backbone and neck
not the same on both sides

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that owls are the best hunters among all birds? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how two of the owl's body features work together to help it catch a mouse in the dark.
struggling: Pre-teach nocturnal, species, and talons with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses predator, vertebrae, and asymmetrical to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
